turn_text: So I've talked to Secretary Bergram quite a bit about this. I've had a call with him for a close to an hour last week talking specifically about the parks. And then I saw him at the State of the Union address and got to visit with him some more. But the thing that I took away from it is how excited the Secretary is to make our parks more accessible and to give Americans a better experience at the parks than they've had in the past. And if you look at the role of the administration is to administer the programs of the federal government. And I don't think they see these cuts to probationary employees as a hindrance to being able to achieve their objectives of making the parks better. And when I say better, I'm talking about new systems to, we don't have this so much in Arkansas, but out west in the big parks when you try to go into a park oftentimes you're sitting in line for a long time. They're actively trying to hire about 5,000 temporary employees for the summer visitation season when the numbers are up so much. But on the other side of that, there is the human aspect of it of people who lost their jobs. And I don't think anybody should be celebrating that somebody's lost their job, particularly these are Members are community who are hardworking. they face to cut. People in the private sector see that quite a bit. I did talk to Secretary Bergham about the specific cuts in Arkansas in the Park Service, and DOI has gotten back to me and my committee and said there were five Park Service employees on the probationary status that were terminated. Four of them were in the Buffalo National River Unit, one at Peeridge Battlefield, and that's it. There weren't any in hot springs, but the data we're still waiting for is the people were offered the fork and the road letter that went out, and I don't know how many people in the park service in Arkansas took the fork and the road to leave. But we have seen some reductions in visitors hour at the visitor center in hot springs, and then the announcement, I guess, of a visitor center closing, one of the visitor centers on the Buffalo River closing. Well, I think that's gonna get resolved. I talked to Secretary Burgum about that and he was a little bit surprised to find out that that happened because he said a lot more people like in Yellowstone were probationary employees that were terminated and said none of the services had been disrupted in big parts like that. So the response I got was we're gonna figure out how to do this and they're also reviewing a lot of these terminations. So I don't know if that means people are going to be rehired. We've certainly seen that with some of the stuff that Doge has done. But at the end of the day, I think it's going to all work out, and Americans are going to actually have a better experience on their federal lands. There's cuts to the forest service, and forestry is something that's very important to me. I'm still the only forester in Congress. I've got a big bill in DC here today that's in Senator Bozeman's committee for hearing the 6R Forest Act.
